title: Segment force-displacement
summary: Load single motion segments (or L1-S1 under follower load) slowly as stated and report stiffness, flexibility, translation or rotation.
simulate: Build the motion segment of the task (intact, posterior elements removed, or disc-only); fix the lower vertebra.
Apply the preload first, then the single test load or displacement of the task; other DOF free unless stated.
Measure at the reference point stated (upper vertebral body centre or disc centre).
Stiffness = slope over the stated range; displacement = translation or rotation at the stated load.
Matrix terms: impose one DOF at a time with the others held, read the reaction on that DOF (diagonal only).

outputs.label: Translational stiffness
outputs.definition: Stiffness = force / translation along the loaded direction, slope over the stated range (N/mm)

outputs.label: Rotational stiffness
outputs.definition: Stiffness = moment / rotation about the loaded axis, slope over the stated range (Nm/deg)

outputs.label: Translation under load
outputs.definition: Translation of the upper vertebra relative to the lower at the stated load (mm)

outputs.label: Rotation under load
outputs.definition: Rotation of the upper vertebra relative to the lower at the stated load (deg)

outputs.label: Bending moment, % of elastic-limit moment
outputs.definition: Flexion moment at the stated % of the elastic-limit angle (10.5°), as % of the moment at that limit

notes: Quasi-static only: Costi 2008 at 0.001 Hz (slowest of 0.001-1 Hz); Amin 2016 and Cannella 2008 use slow 0.1 Hz cycles. Dynamic and failure tests are excluded.
Only diagonal (direct) terms and principal motions; coupling terms stay in bench/tests.
Amin 2016b refs are degeneration grades of the same 14 FSUs as Amin 2016a; Patwardhan 2003 and Renner 2007 share a lab.
agent_prompt: Use your finite element spine model. For each task build the motion segment in its inputs (intact, posterior elements removed, or disc-only; L1-S1 for follower-load tasks), fix the lower vertebra and apply the preload first. Then apply the single test load or imposed displacement given in "load" with the other degrees of freedom free (for 6x6 diagonal terms, hold them fixed). Report stiffness (k_lin N/mm, k_rot Nm/deg) as the slope over the stated range, flexibility (mm/N, deg/Nm), or the translation (mm) or rotation (deg) at the stated load and reference point. For moment_pct, report the flexion moment at the given % of 10.5 deg as % of the moment at 10.5 deg. Each task lists `studies` (whose specimens it uses) and `unit`. Return JSON with one entry per task id, as in answer_format; null for tasks you cannot simulate.
